cs.t: Similar feelings about the Duo. Very little innovation beyond what is offered by Androids. In fact, I feel like there are many foldable Android phones that offer better hardware (Motorola Razr Fold comes to mind). I say this as someone who is a huge Apple Fanboy and got a Duo on release day.
cs.th: MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display and Touch

cs.t: I used the Microsoft Surface Duo, and the experience was terrible. I carry a Pixel 10 Fold, and 90% of the time I use it closed. But when I want to watch a video, or I want to show someone something. The bezel very much ruins that experience. And the Duo went even further by having hidden pixels, which made some UIs completely unusable. That said, I hardly think that foldable is the peak. I'd prefer a rollable phone that I can expand the screen on, with maybe an edge display. And the price is the real kicker. For the vast majority of the Android population, a phone at a price point about $1000 is just a non-starter.

I've wanted a small android phone for a while now too, but partly because I just don't care much for smartphones and want a small  and cheap  option.  Ideally it'd be a pixel so that it should support GrapheneOS. The foldables are such an interesting concept. I actually had a Surface Duo for a while (though a different style of foldable) and really liked it, but I only had one after they were a year old and I could try it out with a used phone for ~$200.
cs.th: I want an iPhone Mini-sized Android phone (2022)

cs.t: Surface Book 2 - gosh, it has been 3 years since I own this thing and I'm still amazed about the hinge design. Surface Duo - while it has tons of flaws on the software level, it looks like a sci-fi device because of how slim it is!
cs.th: Ask HN: What are the best-designed things you've ever used?

cs.t: Things aren't decided by customers only. There are journalists, YouTubers and whole class of influencers who can decided something is shite on a whim. If enough people do so, the tide may change faster then you'd think. It happened to companies with cult following before. It's literally happening to Nike as we speak. Apple has had more flops than hits in recent years. The Vision Pro, the Glass interface, the Duo hinge flaw that will almost certainly end up with a recall. The Apple Watch always listening, now the bangle touch display with nothing innovative to back it up? They don't deliver like they used to. I was their fanboy for 10 years and they did deliver the quality and innovation consistently, I just don't see it anymore. The only thing they have going is the CPU.
cs.th: MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display and Touch
